compatibility: No product data migration or runtime data contract was introduced by the accepted Phase 3 context-governance work.

mayConsume: A later Project Trim continuation may use this accepted capsule as its prior plateau plus a current mainline delta.
mustNotAssume: The capsule is historical accepted truth, not a replacement for current governing authority, source inspection, or Sounding Line acceptance.

governingRequirements: Project Trim v1.0-R1 Sections 17-19 and 24-30; Carry the Logbook continuation plateau
Sounding Line remains the sole RELEASE_GO and protected-merge authority
knownLimitations: Task-local ledgers are derived continuation context and cannot authorize RELEASE_GO or protected merges.
Persistent learning, advisory budget enforcement, fleet telemetry, and model routing remain outside Phase 3.

authority: Project Trim v1.0-R1 Phase 4 governing sections

activeBehavior: Phase 3 continuation startup consumes the accepted Phase 2 capsule and records privacy-safe read, search, and expansion decisions.
Future Project Trim continuations can consume an accepted capsule as a bounded prior plateau.
fallbacks: Changed, partial, low-confidence, exact-text, security, and relevant-mainline conditions require rereading or targeted expansion.

consumers: repository agents and governed validation workflows
seams: Project Trim context packets, task-local continuation ledgers, governed test registry, and Sounding Line authority

limitations: Continuation benchmarks measure source bytes, pointers, and process timing; they do not claim end-to-end task-token savings without comparable live task replays.
